chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Club Ebony, the show, and 'Shine'
summary: The Dancer band played Jack Johnson's Club Ebony for movie stars; his feature was 'Shine' and Bumps Myers was the best-known sideman.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Where did you, where did this band play?
Earl's band?
Yes.
Well we played in a place called 'Club Ebony' which was a club that had initially been opened by Jack Johnson, the prize fighter. We played therefor a long time. I tell you who was in
the show was, you know, Rochester?
Yes.
He was doing a single. He was a dancer. Yes Rochester, Ed Anderson. He was one of the members of the show.
Well now, would this place be like the Cotton Club? Would it be patronized chiefly by white people or was the, of course it wasn't segregated?
No. Movie stars used to come there every night. George Raft, oh many.
Did this band have to play for the show and the dancing?

The show and dancing, yes. We had a pretty long show. Maybe an hour show, an hour and fifteen minute show and then a break and then we'd play for dancing. And then we'd go back and play another show. We'd do about two shows a night. But it was a very nice, it was a nice club. Our hotel where we lived was right upstairs, so we just (... inaudible ...).
To the Dunbar Hotel
Now are you, are you a featured soloist with this band by this time?
Yes. Yes, yes. My feature
was 'Shine'. (LAUGHTER).
Well that was Louis Armstrong's...
Yes. That was my biggest feature then.
But you never sang it?
No. No, I didn't. We just had to play it like kind of Louis' style. About four or five choruses and end up on a high note.
Now was there nobody else in this band that became famous?
In Earl Dancer's band? No. The closest one would be Bumps Myers.
Oh yes.
Now Bumps and Lester Young made some records together. So he must have been pretty good to play against Lester.
Yes, well Bumps lasted quite a long time.
Yes, Bumps...... was with Benny Carter, too...
